definitions.explanation: A senior military officer rank. In the army and air force, equivalent to colonel. In the navy, equivalent to captain. Part of the Japanese military rank system based on three grades: 大 (senior), 中 (middle), and 少 (junior).

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{陸軍|りくぐん}{大佐|たいさ}だった。
{大佐|たいさ}が{部隊|ぶたい}の{指揮|しき}を{執|と}った。
examples.english: The colonel took command of the unit.

examples.japanese: {戦争|せんそう}{映画|えいが}で、{主人公|しゅじんこう}の{大佐|たいさ}が{困難|こんなん}な{作戦|さくせん}を{成功|せいこう}に{導|みちび}いた。
examples.english: In the war movie, the colonel protagonist led a difficult operation to success.

notes:
USAGE:
The Japanese military rank system uses a three-tier structure with {佐|さ} (field officer) grades: {大佐|たいさ} (senior), {中佐|ちゅうさ} (middle), and {少佐|しょうさ} (junior). In the army these correspond to colonel, lieutenant colonel, and major.

In the navy, {大佐|たいさ} corresponds to captain (not to be confused with army captain, which is {大尉|たいい}).

Commonly encountered in war films, historical fiction, and military discussions. Also used when translating foreign military ranks.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {陸軍|りくぐん}{大佐|たいさ}: army colonel
- {海軍|かいぐん}{大佐|たいさ}: navy captain
- {大佐|たいさ}に{昇進|しょうしん}する: to be promoted to colonel
